questions.q: A balloon is moving up in air vertically above a point A on the ground. When it is a height h1, a girl standing at a distance d (point B) from A (see figure) sees it at an angle 45° with respect to the vertical. When the balloon climbs up a further height h2, it is seen at an angle 60° with respect to the vertical if the girl moves further by a distance 2.464 d (point C). Then the height h2 is (given tan30°=0.5774):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
t45=h1d

h1=d   .......(i)

h1+h2d+2.464d=tan30°=13=0.5774

h1+h2=(3.464)d×0.5774

h1+h2=2d   .......(ii)

∴ h2=d

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>150</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The ratio of velocity after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____. {take, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>}
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the velocity of the ball after 3 s is given by

v3=u-3g   ...1

The formula to calculate the velocity of the ball after 5 s is given by

v5=u-5g   ...2

Divide equation (1) by equation (2) to obtain the required ratio.

v3v5=u-3gu-5g   ...3

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

v3v5=150-30150-50=120100=65= 5+15

Comparing the above equation with the given expression, it can be written that x=5.

questions.q:
A NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of 9 km h-1 under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of 19.6 m. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango whose distance from the tree at time of drop is :
(Given g=9.8 m s-2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If a cadet receives the mango, then the time taken by the mango to fall and the cadet to reach there should be equal.

Time taken by mango to fall t=2hg.

⇒t=2×19.69.8=2 s

Therefore, the distance of the cadet from the tree will be, d=vt.

⇒d=9×518×2=5 m

=12×t×v0=12×t×αβtα+β=αβt22(α+β)

questions.q:
The displacement x versus time graph is shown below.

(A) The average velocity during 0 to 3 s is $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(B) The average velocity during 3 to 5 s is $0 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(C) The instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~s}$ is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(D) The average velocity during 5 to 7 s and instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=6.5 \mathrm{~s}$ are equal
(E) The average velocity from $t=0$ to $t=9 \mathrm{~s}$ is zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=\frac{\Delta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{s}}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{i}}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{\mathrm{ds}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\text { slope }
\end{aligned}$
(A) 0 to $3 \mathrm{sec} ;\langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=\frac{5-0}{3}=5 / 3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(B) 0 to $5 \mathrm{sec} ;\langle\vec{v}\rangle=\frac{5-5}{2}=0$
(C) $\mathrm{t}=2 ;$ slope $=\vec{v}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(D) $\mathfrak{t}=5$ to $7 \mathrm{sec} ;\langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=\frac{0-5}{2}=-2.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
At $t=6.5 \mathrm{sec} ; \vec{v}=10$
(E) $\mathrm{t}=0$ to $\mathrm{t}=9 ;\langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=0$

questions.q: A train starting from rest first accelerates uniformly up to a speed of $80 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ for time $t$, then it moves with a constant speed for time $3 t$. The average speed of the train for this duration of journey will be (in $\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{h}$ ) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \text { Average speed } & =\frac{\text { total distance }}{\text { time taken }} \\ & =\frac{\frac{80 \times \mathrm{t}}{2}+80 \times 3 \mathrm{t}}{4 \mathrm{t}}=70 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr} .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, x = 4t2

We know that velocity is the rate at which displacement changes with time. So, v=dxdt=d4t2dt=8t

Now, at t=5 s

Velocity of particle is v=8×5=40 m s-1.

questions.q: An elevator in a building can carry a maximum of <math><mn>10</mn></math> persons, with the average mass of each person being <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>68</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> . The mass of the elevator itself is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>920</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and it moves with a constant speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> . The frictional force opposing the motion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> . If the elevator is moving up with its full capacity, the power delivered by the motor to the elevator <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfenced></math> must be at least:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force on motor will be
Fm=920+6810g+6000
=22000 N
So, required power for motor
Pm=F→m.v→
=22000×3
=66000 watt

The force acts only for the time interval <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>T</mi></math>. The velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> of the particle after time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>T</mi></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A passenger sitting in a train A moving at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> observes another train B moving in the opposite direction for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. If the velocity of the train B is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, then length of train B is:

questions.solution:
Let the velocity of A be vA and the velocity of B be vB.

The relative velocity is

v→BA =v→B-v→A⇒vBA= 54-(-90)=144 km h-1

⇒vBA= 40 m s-1

Time=lengthvBA 

⇒length= 40 m s-1 × 8 s=320 m

questions.q: A juggler throws balls vertically upwards with same initial velocity in air. When the first ball reaches its highest position, he throws the next ball. Assuming the juggler throws <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> balls per second, the maximum height the balls can reach is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the juggler is throwing n balls each second and 2nd when the first is at its highest point, so the time taken by one ball to reach the highest point, t=1n s.

And as at highest point v=0.

So, from first equation of motion,

v=u+at⇒0=u-g1n⇒u=gn

Now in order to calculate height, using second equation of motion, we have:
S=ut+12at2 ...(i)

⇒h=1n×gn-12g×1n2

     ⇒h=g2n2

So, the balls rise up to a height of h=g2n2 m.

questions.q: A particle moves along the $x$-axis and has its displacement $x$ varying with time $t$ according to the equation $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{c}_0\left(\mathrm{t}^2-2\right)+\mathrm{c}(\mathrm{t}-2)^2$ where $c_0$ and $c$ are constants of appropriate dimensions. Then, which of the following statements is correct?
options: the acceleration of the particle is $2 \mathrm{c}_0$
the acceleration of the particle is $2\mathrm{~c}$
the initial velocity of the particle is $4\mathrm{~c}$
the acceleration of the particle is $2\left(c+c_0\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \mathrm{tC}_0+2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{t}-2) \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \mathrm{C}_0+2 \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

The relation between acceleration <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>a</mi></mfenced></math> and velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>v</mi></mfenced></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: t=αx2+βx 

Differentiating w.r.t time, we get

dtdx=2αx+β

⇒1v=2αx+β

Differentiating w.r.t time again, we get

⇒-1v2dvdt=2αdxdt

⇒dvdt=-2αv3as v=dxdt⇒a=dvdt=-2αv3

questions.q: A person travels <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> distance with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> distance with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in the same direction. The average velocity of the person is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math>, then the relation between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> will be
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable columnalign="right left right left right left right left right left right left" columnspacing="0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em" rowspacing="3pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mtd></mtr></mtable></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time t1 taken by the person to travel distance x with velocity v1 is given by

t1=xv1   ...1

The time t2 taken by the person to travel distance x with velocity v2 is given by

t2=xv2   ...2

The formula to calculate the average speed v of the person is given by

v=2xt1+t2   ...3

Substitute the expressions from equations (1) and (2) into equation (3) to obtain the required relation.

v=2xxv1+xv2⇒xv1+xv2=2xv⇒2v=1v1+1v2

questions.q: From the top of a tower, a ball is thrown vertically upward which reaches the ground in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. A second ball thrown vertically downward from the same position with the same speed reaches the ground in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When it is thrown upward, -h=v×6-12g62

Therefore, 5h=536+9 h=45 m

questions.q: A person travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity $\mathrm{v}_1$ for a distance x and with a uniform velocity $\mathrm{v}_2$ for the next $\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{x}$ distance. The average velocity in this motion is $\frac{50}{7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If $\mathrm{v}_1$ is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ then $\mathrm{v}_2=$ _________ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}_{\text {avg }}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_1+\mathrm{x}_2}{\mathrm{t}_1+\mathrm{t}_2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{50}{7}=\frac{\mathrm{x}+\frac{3 \mathrm{x}}{2}}{\frac{\mathrm{x}}{5}+\frac{3 \mathrm{x}}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{50}{7}=\frac{5 / 2}{\frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{7}{20}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{7}{20}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{7-4}{20} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{3}{20} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}_2=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$
